candidate.selection_reason: User-uploaded file content -> JSON.parse without validation -> potential prototype pollution or object injection
candidate.source_summary: records parameter comes from _text which is file content read via fs.readFile from uploaded .etherpad files processed through formidable file upload handler
candidate.sink_summary: Parsed JSON objects are written to database via db.set() calls for each key-value pair after rewriting padId in keys
candidate.guard_summary: No validation, sanitization, or schema checking of JSON content before parsing; file extension check (.etherpad) but no content validation
candidate.risk_pattern: User-uploaded file content directly parsed as JSON without validation, then written to database keys and values
candidate.context_summary: HTTP POST /p/:pad/import -> formidable file upload -> .etherpad file content -> JSON.parse -> database writes
unresolved_facts: Exact database schema and impact of arbitrary key-value writes
Whether db.set() performs any validation or escaping
Presence of other security controls in database layer

target_cwe.cwe_name: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection')
target_cwe.description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before it is used as an identifier for a resource that may be outside the intended sphere of control. A resource injection issue occurs when the following two conditions are met: An attacker can specify the identifier used to access a system resource. For example, an attacker might...
remediation_steps: Use parameterized queries and prepared statements
Implement strict input validation with whitelisting

stage3_hypothesis.cwe_name: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection')
stage3_hypothesis.fit_reason: User-controlled JSON keys become database keys (resource identifiers) without validation, allowing injection into database resource paths.
